approach.expect: From the Gorge Creek Overlook pull-off on Highway 20 (about 1,100 ft, roughly 2.6 miles/4.2 km east of Newhalem), cross the metal footbridge over Gorge Creek and immediately leave the maintained overlook trail — there is no numbered or maintained trail beyond the bridge, so the rest of the approach is off-trail route-finding by boot-track, cairns, and game trails up Davis Peak's south/southwest flank. The lower forest (partly within a 2015 burn) is steep and brushy with deadfall and blowdown; an animal-path line generally holds up through open timber. Around 2,400-2,800 ft, cliff bands force a bypass (parties generally work right); continue up steep timber to roughly 3,600-3,800 ft, where a brushy gully and intermittent animal paths lead through more open woods. Near 4,000 ft a partly snow-filled gully, and around 4,500 ft a talus draw, mark the transition out of forest; granite slabs and alpine snowfields begin around 4,800-4,850 ft, where the angle eases as the terrain flattens onto the crest of the southwest ridge. Stay left/north of Point 5,872 (a subpeak on Davis's east ridge, sometimes called "Little Davie," ~6,240 ft) rather than committing to its slopes - multiple parties have found avalanche-prone snow there in shoulder-season conditions and turned back - and climb snow/talus to the broad notch/saddle at roughly 5,700-5,800 ft on the south ridge (about 4-4.5 hours from the car for a fit party). There is no reliable water past the lower forest, so fill up at Gorge Creek near the trailhead. Total distance is roughly 6-8 miles round trip with about 5,900 ft of gain from trailhead to the 7,054 ft summit, almost all of it off-trail through brush, talus, and low-5th-class-adjacent terrain. A longer alternate approach follows the primitive Stetattle Creek Trail about 2 miles from Diablo, then leaves the trail, drops about 200 ft to ford Stetattle Creek, and climbs the peak's north/west side - but as of 2026 the Stetattle Creek Trail is fully closed by NPS due to 2023 Sourdough Fire damage (standing dead trees/debris), so this alternate is not currently usable; plan on the Gorge Creek Overlook approach instead.

approach.expect: From the Downey Creek Trailhead (1,400', end of the drivable Suiattle River Road/FR-26 — note the road itself is currently gated by a washout about 4.5 miles short of the actual trailhead, adding road-walking/biking mileage many trip reports don't separate from the hike), follow Downey Creek Trail #768. The maintained tread climbs gently along Downey Creek, crossing five tributary creeks (one draining Downey/Pilot Lakes can be a difficult ford in spring high water) and passing informal camps at roughly 1.6, 3, 3.5, and 4 miles before reaching the Bachelor Creek crossing at 6.6 miles/2,400'. Expect old-growth blowdown across the tread in places and a brushy avalanche-chute crossing opposite Green Mountain. At Bachelor Creek, leave the maintained trail and pick up the unmaintained Bachelor Creek climbers'/boot path, which follows the north side of the creek (parties report an improved use-trail here that avoids older brushy sections) up to Bachelor Flats and Bachelor Meadows — the common first-night camp, roughly 10-12 miles and most parties' Day 1 stop. From Bachelor Meadows continue up steepening open slopes to Cub Pass, then drop about 700' to Cub Lake and cross the meadows beyond it to gain Itswoot Ridge/Itswoot Pass. From Itswoot Pass, step onto the Dome Glacier and rope up for crevasse-hazard glacier travel, traversing to the broad Chikamin-Dome col (~8,500'), a well-established, wind-sheltered camp used as a high camp by most parties (roughly 17 miles and 7,000'+ gain from the trailhead to this point). From the col, a further descending traverse (roughly 90 minutes) drops onto the Chikamin Glacier to a snow bench/rock outcrop around 7,000-7,500' directly below Gunsight's west face — many parties move camp here or simply day-climb from the col. Route-finding on the unmaintained Bachelor Creek path and Cub Pass/Itswoot Ridge sections, plus crevasse hazard on the Dome and Chikamin Glaciers, are the main approach-specific concerns; carry a rope, crevasse rescue gear, and be comfortable with off-trail alpine travel.

From Itswoot Pass, step onto the Dome Glacier and rope up for crevasse-hazard glacier travel, traversing to the broad Chikamin-Dome col (~8,500'), a well-established, wind-sheltered camp used as a high camp by most parties (roughly 17 miles and 7,000'+ gain from the trailhead to this point). From the col, a further descending traverse (roughly 90 minutes) drops onto the Chikamin Glacier to a snow bench/rock outcrop around 7,000-7,500' directly below Gunsight's west face — many parties move camp here or simply day-climb from the col. Route-finding on the unmaintained Bachelor Creek path and Cub Pass/Itswoot Ridge sections, plus crevasse hazard on the Dome and Chikamin Glaciers, are the main approach-specific concerns; carry a rope, crevasse rescue gear, and be comfortable with off-trail alpine travel.
